title: Bits and Bytes
blurb: Strange true stories from video games, the internet and computing history.

prompts.text: In 1947 engineers taped a real _____ into the logbook of the Harvard Mark II computer as the first actual case of a bug being found.
Atari took its name from a term in the board game _____.
Nintendo began in 1889 making traditional Japanese playing cards called _____.
In the original arcade game Donkey Kong, the hero we now call Mario was named _____.
Sony's PlayStation began as a CD add-on planned for the Super Famicom, a console made by _____.
Ray Tomlinson sent the first networked email in 1971 and chose the _____ symbol to separate the user name from the computer name.
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at the physics lab _____.
Before it was Google, the search engine's original name was _____.
Jeff Bezos first incorporated Amazon in 1994 under the name _____.
Jack Dorsey's first tweet in 2006 read "just setting up my _____".
The first video ever uploaded to YouTube, in 2005, was titled "Me at the _____".
The first computer mouse prototype, built in the 1960s by Douglas Engelbart's team, had a shell made of _____.
The name Tetris blends the Greek word for four with the sport _____.
Microsoft bought Mojang, the maker of Minecraft, in 2014 for about $_____ billion.
During development the Nintendo Wii went by the codename _____.
The princess in The Legend of Zelda was named after the wife of author F. Scott _____.
Pokemon creator Satoshi Tajiri based the idea on his childhood hobby of collecting _____.
Nokia began in 1865 as a _____ mill.
The Apple I computer went on sale in 1976 for the price of $_____.
The first .com domain name ever registered, in 1985, was _____.com.
Bluetooth is named after a 10th century king of _____.
Linus Torvalds announced Linux in 1991 as "just a _____, won't be big and professional like gnu".
The first ever text message, sent in December 1992, said "Merry _____".
The world's first webcam, at Cambridge University, pointed at a _____ pot so researchers could check if it was empty.
The first message sent over ARPANET in 1969 was meant to be "LOGIN" but the system crashed after the letters "_____".
IBM's Deep Blue became the first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion, Garry Kasparov, in a full match in _____.
In North America the Game Boy launched in 1989 bundled with the game _____.
Sega's Genesis console was sold in Japan and Europe as the Mega _____.
In the name CAPTCHA, the T stands for the _____ test.
In 2010 a programmer famously paid _____ bitcoin for two pizzas.
The mobile game Angry Birds was created by a company from _____.
The hit mobile game Flappy Bird was created by developer Dong Nguyen of _____.
Google's first ever Doodle, in 1998, announced that its founders had gone to the _____ festival.
Microsoft's paperclip assistant, widely known as Clippy, was officially named _____.
Ada Lovelace, often called the first computer programmer, was the daughter of the poet Lord _____.
In Japan, Pac-Man was originally called _____-Man.
Minecraft was created by Markus Persson, better known online as "_____".
Apple's original 1976 logo showed Sir Isaac _____ sitting under an apple tree.
Microsoft was founded in 1975 in the New Mexico city of _____.
Apple's famous "1984" Macintosh ad, aired during the Super Bowl, was directed by Ridley _____.
The first item ever sold on eBay was a broken _____.
Skype's software was created by a team of developers from the small country of _____.
The mascot of the Linux operating system is a penguin named _____.
The Python programming language takes its name from the BBC comedy series Monty Python's _____ Circus.
The programming language Java was first named after a tree outside its creator's office, and was called _____.
